title: Measuring the Money Returned on a Withdrawn Ridgecrest Advantage Application
content:
The money returned on a withdrawn Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan application is measured from the payments standing on that application's premium account, and how many of them stand there settles which measure is taken.

| Payments standing on the application's premium account | The money returned on the application |
| --- | --- |
| At least 3 | Every payment posted to that account |
| Exactly 2 | The payments posted to that account in the last 3 months |
| Fewer than 2, that is 0 or 1 | The most recent payment posted to it |

The three rows divide the whole range of possibilities between them: with 3 or more payments every payment counts, with exactly 2 only those inside the last 3 months count, and with 1 or none only the most recent counts.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

*An application whose premium account carries 4 payments of 50.00, 60.00, 70.00 and 80.00 USD.* At least 3 payments stand there, so every payment counts, and the money returned is 260.00 USD.

*An application whose premium account carries exactly 2 payments, of 90.00 USD posted five months ago and 110.00 USD posted last month.* Only the payments posted inside the last 3 months count, so the money returned is 110.00 USD.

*An application whose premium account carries 1 payment of 47.60 USD.* Fewer than 2 payments stand there, so the most recent payment is what is returned: 47.60 USD.
